author: agent:claude-code
message: Flat::update patches instead of rebuilding: the forest logs what changed, and the view writes those child lists again and walks only the subtrees under them. A change deep in the tree now costs 1.5 / 3.2 us at 10k / 100k nodes (a reorder ~105 ns) against a 20 / 340 us rebuild; a randomized test checks every patch against a fresh rebuild. Version 0.1.1 for release. (proposal 01a15bad-5aad-7189-a7b4-822c28e4014b, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

check.name: a patched Flat matches a rebuilt one

title: Flat patches from a change log the forest keeps
body: The forest logs each parent whose child list changed (NONE for the roots; a run of changes to one parent is one entry) and each freed slot, bounded at 4096 entries (the oldest half goes). Flat::update re-reads from the last entry it saw (a later change may have merged into it), writes the changed lists again at the end of its packed child lists, then walks again only the subtrees under changed slots with no changed ancestor, each found at its old position by stepping down from the roots over earlier siblings' ends, and splices them in from the last to the first, shifting what follows when one grew or shrank. It rebuilds instead when the roots changed, the log has moved past it, a subtree can't be placed or two overlap, or stale list entries outnumber live ones. benches/forest.rs: a child added or removed deep in the tree and update, 1.5 / 3.2 us at 10k / 100k; a deep reorder, ~105 ns; a full rebuild 20 / 340 us. Checked by a_patched_flat_matches_a_rebuilt_one: 4000 batches of random inserts, moves, reorders and removals, each compared with a fresh rebuild (preorder, ends, child lists, skipping walk); breaking the ancestors' end fix-up or the shift after a region each fails it at step 0. The log's cost on builds: at 10k within the noise (with it switched off, 117-129 us against 121-141 us), at 100k about 4% (936-942 us against 903-906 us).

title: Building 10k nodes depends on the machine's state
body: The same code (the commit before the change log, run as a control) measured 69 us in one session and 115-125 us in another, while the arena measured 62-73 us both times; at 100k the forest stays at 0.9-1.0 ms against the arena's 1.0-1.1 ms. Likely first-touch page faults on the forest's up-front allocation, which the arena's many small allocations avoid. A caller that builds once and changes the tree (a UI) pays it once.
